# FRAME: shift swaps for nurses

## Job statement
When a planned shift no longer fits my life, a hospital nurse wants to hand it to a colleague quickly, so they can keep
their commitments without leaving the ward short.

## Problem
How might we help nurses trade shifts safely for the ward so that coverage never drops below the safe minimum?
Swaps are arranged by phone and on paper today, and the charge nurse learns about them late.

## Audience / boundary
Registered nurses and charge nurses on inpatient wards of one hospital.

## Success looks like
Most swaps are agreed and approved within one working day. Baseline: NOT VERIFIED.

## Hard constraints (gates)
- Staffing rules of the ward are never broken.
- Staff data stays inside the hospital's approved region.

## Soft constraints
- Works on the phones and desk computers the staff already use.

## Non-goals
- Payroll changes.
- Automatic rostering.

## Decision ledger
| # | decision | answer | status |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Scope | one hospital | CONFIRMED |

## Premises
- P1 Swaps happen every week on every ward. NOT VERIFIED (ask two charge nurses).

## Kill condition for the whole effort
Charge nurses refuse any tool that bypasses their approval.

## Criteria
- Value 30: 1 = nobody notices, 3 = saves some calls, 5 = swaps take minutes
- Feasibility 25: 1 = needs new systems, 3 = needs one integration, 5 = works with what exists
- Fit 20: 1 = fights ward culture, 3 = neutral, 5 = matches how wards work
- Distinctiveness 15: 1 = the obvious answer, 3 = a twist, 5 = far from the obvious answer
- Evidence 10: 1 = none, 3 = anecdotes, 5 = observed data

## Kill rules
K1-K6 as in the skill.

## Axes
- Moment: planning, handover, night shift
- Channel: mobile, desk, paper
- Actor: nurse, charge nurse, coordinator

## Strategy plan
S1-S5 as seated by the engine.

## Mode, privacy, budget
standard; privacy (a) yes, (b) no; one week.
